conventions.convention: The standard complex inner product is linear in its first argument; vector norms are Euclidean and matrix norms are induced operator 2-norms.
Phi indices start at k=0, with φ_k(X)=Σ_{j≥0}X^j/(j+k)! and X^0=I. Zero-dimensional matrices are admitted; their identity and operator norm are zero.
The logarithmic norm is μ₂(A)=λ_max((A+A*)/2), defined only for n≥1; it may be negative.
The action defect is r=Au−u′. Complex vector integrals are oriented componentwise Riemann integrals after realification.
Arithmetic certificates are supplied mathematical contracts with exactly represented nonnegative rational bounds; no particular floating-point kernel is asserted to satisfy them.

Happy breakdown requires exact zero residual or a verified full exact Arnoldi-recurrence certificate. A small computed subdiagonal alone is numerical breakdown. Relation, reduced-action, and projection statuses are separate.
For negative action time, the residual bound uses μ₂(−A), integrates over [t,0], and uses the nonnegative distance |t−s|.

load_bearing.statement: For every integer k≥0, the scalar series defining φ_k(z) converges absolutely for every z∈ℂ, and the matrix series defining φ_k(X) converges absolutely in operator 2-norm for every X∈M_n(ℂ), n≥0. At zero, φ_k(0)=1/k! and φ_k(0_{n×n})=I_n/k!.

Let n≥1, A∈M_n(ℂ), T>0, v∈ℂ^n, and u:[−T,T]→ℂ^n be continuously differentiable, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints. With r(s)=Au(s)−u′(s), for every t∈[−T,T], e^{tA}v−u(t)=e^{tA}(v−u(0))+∫₀ᵗe^{(t−s)A}r(s)ds.
For n≥1 and A∈M_n(ℂ), H_A=(A+A*)/2 is Hermitian, its eigenvalues are real, and μ₂(A)=λ_max(H_A)=max_{‖x‖₂=1} Re⟨Ax,x⟩.
For A∈M_n(ℂ), n≥1, and τ≥0, ‖e^{τA}‖₂≤e^{τμ₂(A)}. Consequently, for t≤0, ‖e^{tA}‖₂≤e^{|t|μ₂(−A)}. No normality, spectral stability, or sign assumption on μ₂(A) is required.

For every integer k≥0, z∈ℂ, and X∈M_n(ℂ), n≥0, φ_k(z)=1/k!+zφ_{k+1}(z) and φ_k(X)=I_n/k!+Xφ_{k+1}(X). For k≥1 and w∈ℂ^n, with J_k the superdiagonal nilpotent shift and B_k(X,w)=[[X,we₁*],[0,J_k]], the first n entries of e^{B_k(X,w)}[0;e_k] equal φ_k(X)w.

For A∈M_n(ℂ), n≥1, v∈ℂ^n, β≥0, V∈M_{n×m}(ℂ), H∈M_m(ℂ), and 1≤m≤n, put c(s)=e^{sH}βe₁ and u(s)=Vc(s). For every real t, e^{tA}v−u(t)=e^{tA}(v−βVe₁)+∫₀ᵗe^{(t−s)A}(AV−VH)c(s)ds, with an oriented integral. Whenever AV=VH and v=βVe₁, φ_k(tA)v=βVφ_k(tH)e₁ for every k≥0 and every real t.

concerns.concern: Procedure Step 4 leaves reduced_action_status unassigned on a reachable branch. It says to set it to inconclusive if either certificate is missing, then: “Set `reduced_action_status=success` only when the Taylor status and scaling certificate both succeed.” A Taylor call can return a candidate and a finite valid bound with status inconclusive-roundoff because its bound exceeds tolerance. If the subsequent scaling certificate is valid, neither stated assignment applies. Step 5 does not assign this status. The specified output therefore lacks a value on this branch; an explicit otherwise-inconclusive assignment is needed.
